body.name: TxLens
body.description: TxLens provides live, verifiable answers to on-chain and market questions from authoritative sources. Covering 123 intents across blockchain, finance, weather, content, security, and general intelligence domains—each answer includes source attribution and fetch timestamps for transparency.

endpoints.description: ONCHAIN_TX_LOOKUP. Answers "is transaction 0xabc... confirmed or did it fail", "what did this tx hash do", "what is the status of this transaction on Base". Takes a specific transaction reference and returns its details, status and effects: confirmed, reverted, pending or not_found, plus from, to, value_wei, value_eth, block_number, block_hash, receipt_status, and the decoded contract method where the calldata identifies one. Confidence scales with confirmation depth. Params: tx_hash (required, 0x-prefixed, 64 hex characters), chain (optional, one of eth, base, arbitrum, polygon, default eth).

GAS_PRICE. Answers "what is gas right now on Ethereum", "how much does a transfer cost on Polygon", "are fees high on Base". Returns the current transaction fee level on a named chain in wei and gwei, plus the estimated USD cost of a standard 21,000-gas transfer. This is the fee to transact, not the price of the chain's token, which is CRYPTO_PRICE. Params: chain (optional, one of eth, base, arbitrum, polygon, default eth).

WALLET_BALANCE_CHECK. Answers "how much ETH does 0xabc... hold", "what is the USDC balance of this address on Arbitrum". Takes a specific blockchain address and returns its current native-coin or ERC-20 token balance on a named chain. Params: address (required, 0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters), chain (optional, one of eth, base, arbitrum, polygon, default eth), token (optional, 0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters, an ERC-20 contract address; when supplied, returns that token's balance instead of the chain's native coin).

TOKEN_HOLDER_COUNT. Answers "how many wallets hold this token", "how many distinct addresses own 0xabc...". Takes a specific token contract address and returns the count of distinct holding addresses. This is a holder count, not price, supply or market data. Params: token (required, 0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters), chain (optional, one of eth, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, default eth).

TVL_LOOKUP. Answers "what is the TVL of Aave", "how much value is locked in Uniswap", "what is total value locked on Ethereum". Takes a named DeFi protocol, pool or chain and returns the total value locked in it in USD. This is value locked, not market capitalisation. When both a protocol and a chain are supplied it returns that protocol's TVL on that chain alongside its total across all chains. Params: exactly one of protocol (a DefiLlama protocol slug, e.g. "uniswap") or tvl_chain (a free-text DefiLlama chain name, e.g. "Ethereum", covering DefiLlama's ~460 chains rather than only the five EVM chains above, which is why the param name differs from `chain`).

CRYPTO_PRICE. Answers "what is Bitcoin worth", "price of ETH in USD", "how much is the token at 0xabc... trading for". Names a cryptocurrency asset and returns its current USD price, with 24-hour change and market cap where the feed supplies them, cross-checked across independent sources and reported with a source count. For the cost of transacting on a chain use GAS_PRICE instead. Params: either coin_id alone, or price_chain together with token. Exactly one of those two modes. Any coin named in words goes in coin_id, including a coin that shares its name with a chain: ether or Ethereum is coin_id="ethereum", and likewise "bitcoin", "solana". price_chain is only for pricing one specific contract, is never sent on its own, and always needs token (0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters, the token's contract address) alongside it, as in price_chain="base" with the contract to price. It also answers what a coin was worth on a past day: send that day as date ("2023-01-01"), in either mode, and the answer is the price on that date rather than the price now. Leave date off for the current price.

STOCK_PRICE. Answers "what is Apple trading at", "current share price of TSLA", "how much is NVDA stock". Names a listed equity or ticker and returns its current USD share price. It also answers what a stock was worth on a past day, such as "what did NVDA close at on 15 January 2024": send that day as date and the answer is the closing price on it, naming the last trading day before it when the market was shut that day. Params: ticker (required, a stock symbol, e.g. "AAPL") and date (optional, a past day as "2024-01-15"; leave it off for the current price).

SSL_VERIFICATION. Answers "is the SSL certificate for example.com valid", "when does this domain's TLS certificate expire", "who issued the certificate for this host". Takes a hostname and reports the certificate that host is actually serving right now, from a real live TLS handshake performed at request time rather than a cached or certificate-transparency lookup, which disagree whenever a host still serves an old certificate. Reports a named verdict (valid, expired, self_signed, hostname_mismatch, untrusted), issuer, validity window, days to expiry, how many certificates the server presented and whether the chain reaches a trusted root, which name on the certificate the request matched, and the TLS version and cipher actually negotiated, flagging deprecated TLS 1.0/1.1 that will fail for modern clients whatever the certificate says. Params: domain (required, a bare hostname such as "example.com", a full URL, a host:port pair, or a question naming the domain).

WEATHER_FORECAST. Answers "what's the weather in Tokyo the next three days", "will it rain in London tomorrow", "how windy will it be in Cape Town on Friday", "will it snow in Oslo next week", and coordinate forms such as "what is the forecast at latitude 14.6042, longitude 120.9822 in 44 hours?". Accepts coordinates written out in full ("latitude 14.6042, longitude 120.9822"), a compact "lat,lon" pair, a place name, or the whole question, and answers the specific thing asked: the day or window named (right now, today, tonight, tomorrow, a weekday, this weekend, this week, in N hours, the next N days or hours) and the aspect emphasised (rain, wind, snow, storm, freeze, temperature), leading with a direct yes or no on that aspect the way a person would answer, then giving the expected condition in plain words, temperature range, precipitation total and chance of precipitation, snowfall, and peak wind speed with gusts and direction. Read live from the forecast service at request time. Params: location (required, coordinates in either form, a place name, or a whole question), days (optional, 1-16), when (optional, overrides the window parsed from the question), focus (optional, one of rain, wind, snow, storm, freeze, temperature).

STORM_ALERT. Reports storm risk at a location over a stated window, answering questions of the form "what is the storm risk at latitude 14.6042, longitude 120.9822 in 44 hours?" and "what is the storm risk at latitude -5.1486, longitude 119.4319 right now?", as well as "is there a storm risk in Miami this weekend". Reports exactly what such a question asks for: wind speed, gusts, precipitation, and an overall risk between 0 and 1. Accepts coordinates written out in full ("latitude 14.6042, longitude 120.9822"), a compact "lat,lon" pair, a place name, or the whole question, and reads the window from it ("right now", "in N hours", "over the next 48 hours", "this weekend"). Alongside the 0-1 risk score a contract can threshold on, it returns a disruption grade (LOW/MODERATE/HIGH/SEVERE) from peak wind gust and its Beaufort force named in plain words, sustained wind speed and direction, total precipitation, forecast thunderstorm and hail hours, and the operational response that grade calls for. The window runs from the current hour forward, not from midnight, so the peak gust reported is always still ahead. Read live at request time. Params: location (required, coordinates in either form, a place name, or a whole question), hours (optional, default 48, also read from the question).

IP_GEOLOCATION. Answers "where is 8.8.8.8 located", "what country is this IP address from", "is this IP a VPN or a datacenter". Takes an IPv4 or IPv6 address and reports its country, region, city, postal code, coordinates, timezone, and network owner with ASN, plus privacy and risk flags saying whether the address is a known proxy or VPN exit, a hosting or datacenter network, or a mobile carrier network, which is what fraud, bot-screening and geo-gating callers actually need. Read live at request time. Confidence is reported as 0.95 rather than 1.0 because IP geolocation is reliable to the country and only approximate to the city. Params: ip (required, a bare IPv4 or IPv6 address such as "8.8.8.8" or "2001:4860:4860::8888", or a whole question naming one).

ACADEMIC_SEARCH. Answers "find papers on federated learning", "peer-reviewed research on fraud detection since 2020". Takes a topic, or the whole question, and lists peer-reviewed journal articles on it in relevance order, with preprints, theses and datasets excluded, naming every paper found in the answer itself with its title, authors, publishing journal, year, citation count and DOI, plus a real excerpt from the leading paper's abstract and a note on which of the results is the most cited. A date range stated in the question ("since 2020", "between 2010 and 2020") is applied. Read live from OpenAlex, with Crossref as a fallback, at request time. Params: topic (required), limit (optional, 1-25, default 5), from_year (optional), to_year (optional).

WEB_SEARCH. Answers an open question of any kind from a live web search performed at request time, for questions that have no single authoritative feed behind them: "what happened at the summit this week", "how does a heat pump work", "will El Nino disrupt shipping this season", "what did the company announce". Takes the whole question as the caller wrote it and returns a direct written answer followed by the sources it drew on, naming the most relevant three with their URLs. Questions about current events are searched against a news index and questions about markets and company results against a finance index, chosen from the wording of the question itself. Confidence is reported as 0.9 rather than 1.0 because a synthesized web answer is only as reliable as the pages behind it, unlike a chain read or a live TLS handshake. For a peer-reviewed literature search use ACADEMIC_SEARCH instead, and for a live number such as a price, gas fee, balance or forecast use the specific intent for it, which reads the value from its own provider rather than from the open web. Params: query (required, the whole question), max_results (optional, 1-20, default 5), topic_mode (optional, one of general, news, finance, overriding what the question implies).

CONTENT_EXTRACTION. Answers "what does this page say", "extract the text from this URL", "summarize the content at this link". Fetches a live URL at request time and returns its title and readable text, stripped of scripts, navigation, and markup. Params: url (required, a full http or https URL, a bare host such as github.com/torvalds, or a whole question containing one; also accepted as link or question). If the value is a passage of text with no URL, the dates, quantities, named entities and events are extracted from the text itself.

TEXT_CLASSIFICATION. Answers "what category is this text", "is this email spam or not", "classify this review as positive or negative". Takes a piece of text and returns the single best category it belongs to, with a brief reason. Params: text (required; also accepted as content or input), labels (optional, also accepted as categories or classes; comma-separated candidate categories the answer must pick from; if omitted, the category is chosen freely).

TEXT_GENERATION. Answers "write a short bio for a software engineer", "draft a product description for a water bottle". Takes an instruction or prompt and writes the requested text directly, with no preamble. Params: prompt (required).

LANGUAGE_GENERATION. Answers "translate this into French", "rewrite this in a formal tone", "paraphrase this sentence". Takes existing text and transforms it into another language, tone, or style. Params: text (required), target (optional, the target language/tone/style; also read from the instruction inside text when omitted).

RESEARCH_SYNTHESIS. Answers broader research questions such as "what are the main approaches to carbon capture" or "summarize the current state of quantum error correction". Combines multiple live web sources into one written synthesis, wider and more source-dense than WEB_SEARCH. Params: query (required; also q, question, topic, text), max_sources (optional, 1-20, default 10; also max_results, limit).

CROSS_CHAIN_STATE_VERIFY. Answers "which chains is this address active on", "does this wallet exist on Base and Arbitrum", "is this a contract on any chain". Checks the same address's native balance and contract status on every supported chain at once. Params: address (required, 0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters), chains (optional, comma-separated list restricting which chains are checked; defaults to every RPC-enabled chain). Chains named in the question ("on Base and Arbitrum") restrict the check when chains is omitted; chains this miner cannot read (Solana, Bitcoin, Optimism) are named as unchecked in the answer.

EVENT_OUTCOME_RESOLUTION. Answers "did the merger go through", "who won the election", "was the proposal approved". Resolves a question about whether something happened to a stated outcome from a live web search, leading with the verdict (yes/no/winner) before the supporting facts. Params: query (required; also q, question, event, market). Answer leads with "Yes,", "No,", the winner's name, or "Not yet resolved," for events that have not happened; the outcome field carries yes/no/unresolved.

WEATHER_CHECK. Answers "what's the weather like in Tokyo right now", "current temperature in London", "is it raining in Cape Town at the moment". Returns a single live current-conditions reading at a named place: temperature, apparent temperature, humidity, wind speed and direction, precipitation, cloud cover, and plain-words condition, read live at request time rather than forecast. Params: location (required, a place name, "lat,lon" pair, or a whole question naming the place; also accepted as city, place, q, query or question, or as lat/lon or latitude/longitude).

LANGUAGE_TRANSLATION. Answers "translate 'good morning' into Japanese", "how do you say thank you in French". Takes text and a target language and returns the translation only, with no explanation. Params: text (required; a whole instruction such as "Translate 'good morning' into Spanish" is accepted and the language is read from it), target (optional when the text names the language; also accepted as target_language, to, language or langpair such as "en|de").

CHAT_COMPLETION. Answers a message directly and conversationally, the way a chat assistant would, with no preamble. A "will X happen" question is answered with a verdict word (Likely, Unlikely, Uncertain) followed by the reason. Params: message (required; also accepted as prompt, text, question, query, or an OpenAI-style messages array whose last user turn is answered).

NEWS_SEARCH. Answers "what's the latest on the trade talks", "has the company announced results yet" from a live news-focused web search at request time, with sources named. Params: query (required; also q, question, topic, text, search, keywords, subject, category), max_results (optional, 1-20, default 5; also max, limit), recent_days (optional, default 7), country and language (optional hints).

NEWS_HEADLINES. Answers "what are today's headlines on the election", "top news about the central bank". Returns a short list of current headlines on a named topic, each with its source URL. Params: topic (required; also query, q, question, category, subject, keywords; a whole question such as "What are the top news headlines about X today?" is accepted), max_results (optional, 1-10, default 6; also max, limit, count). Returns headlines as [{title, source, published, url}].

FACT_CHECK. Answers "is it true that X", "fact check this claim: ...". Checks a stated claim against live web sources and returns a True/False/Unverified verdict with the reasoning and sources behind it. Params: claim (required; also statement, text, query, q, question). Returns verdict (True, False, Mostly True, Mostly False, Misleading, Unverified) and the graded answer leads with that verdict word.

SENTIMENT_ANALYSIS. Answers "is this review positive or negative", "what's the sentiment of this message". Classifies text as exactly one of Positive, Negative, Neutral or Mixed, with a short reason. Also answers "what is the general sentiment toward X" for a named company, token or event. Params: text (required; also accepted as content, review, message or comment).

CONTENT_MODERATION. Answers "does this text violate policy", "is this message safe to post". Judges text as Safe or Flagged against common platform policies (hate speech, harassment, threats, illegal activity), with a short reason naming the concern. Params: text (required; also accepted as content, message, comment or post).

CVE_LOOKUP. Answers "what is CVE-2021-44228", "known vulnerabilities in log4j". Takes a CVE id or a keyword and returns matching vulnerability records from the National Vulnerability Database, with description, severity score, and references. Params: cve (required, a CVE id such as "CVE-2021-44228", a sentence containing one, or a product keyword such as "log4j"; also accepted as cve_id, id, vulnerability, query or question).

TELEGRAPH_KNOWLEDGE. Answers general-knowledge questions and questions about Telegraph Protocol itself, grounded against telegraphprotocol.com for protocol-specific questions rather than guessing about a protocol the model was not trained on. Params: question (required, also accepted as query, q, text, input).
TEXT_SUMMARIZATION. Summarizes supplied text to a given length or style, or a sensible default when none is named. Params: text (required), length (optional, e.g. "50 words" or "one sentence").

CHATBOT_CONVERSATION. Replies to a chat message, using a supplied messages/history array as context when given. Params: message (required), messages (optional, a JSON array of {role, content} turns, also accepted as history).
SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY. Returns a 0-1 semantic similarity score and a short reason for two supplied texts. Params: text1, text2 (required, also accepted as a and b).
GRAMMAR_SPELL_CHECK. Returns corrected text plus a count and list of the grammar and spelling fixes made. Params: text (required).

AI_TEXT_DETECTION. Returns an approximate self-assessment of how likely supplied text is AI-generated, with named cues and an honest disclaimer that this is a language-model estimate, not a certified detector. Params: text (required).

RESEARCH_QUERY. Answers an open research question from live web sources in one well-sourced paragraph. Params: query (required, also accepted as q, question, topic, text, research, search, prompt, subject), max_results (optional, 1-20, default 6).

THREAT_INTELLIGENCE. Given an IP, domain, file hash, CVE id, or threat actor/malware family name, reports whether it is a known threat: malicious/clean verdict and pulse count from AlienVault OTX for IPs/domains/hashes, exploitation status and CVSS severity from CIRCL/NVD for CVE ids, or a web-search-sourced profile for actor and malware-family names. Params: indicator (required, also accepted as ioc, ip, domain, hash, cve, actor, query, q, question, text, input).

PACKAGE_STATUS. Given a shipment tracking number, reports its current status via live web search, since no free universal carrier API exists; answers honestly when no authoritative status can be found rather than guessing. Params: tracking_number (required, also accepted as tracking, tracking_id, number, package_id, query, q, question, text, input).

URL_SCAN. Given a URL, returns a Safe/Suspicious/Unknown verdict combining live reachability and redirect-chain checking, TLS certificate validity, and a web-search reputation check for phishing/malware/scam reports. Params: url (required, also accepted as link, website, target, query, q, question, text, input).

CURRENCY_EXCHANGE. Answers "how much is 100 dollars in euros", "convert 50 GBP to JPY", using live ECB reference rates. Params: from, to (currency codes or names such as "dollars", "euros"), amount (optional, default 1).

FX_NOW. Answers "what is the USD to EUR rate right now", "current GBP JPY exchange rate", "how much is 250 dollars in naira today" with the current mid-market rate from a live FX feed covering 166 currencies, falling back to the ECB reference rate. Params: from (also base), to (also symbols, quote_currency), both currency codes or names such as "dollars", "euros"; amount (optional, default 1); or the whole question as query.

SANCTIONS_SCREENING_MATCH. Answers "is John Doe sanctioned", "check this company against the OFAC list". Screens a name against the US Treasury OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list with fuzzy matching. Params: name (required, a person or entity name).

VULNERABILITY_TRIAGE. Answers "how urgent is CVE-2021-44228", "should I patch log4j now". Same CIRCL/NVD CVE data as CVE_LOOKUP, framed as a triage decision: severity tier, CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities status, and a recommended remediation urgency. Params: cve (required, a CVE id or product keyword).

SPORTS_SCORE. Answers "what is the score of the Lakers game". Most recent or in-progress score for a named team, via TheSportsDB, with a live web-search fallback for teams outside its coverage. Params: team (required, a club or franchise name).

GAME_RESULT. Answers "who won the Knicks game". Winner of a named team's most recently completed match, via TheSportsDB, with a live web-search fallback for teams outside its coverage. Params: team (required, a club or franchise name).

ROUTE_ETA. Answers "how long to drive from London to Paris", "what is the distance between Miami and Orlando". Driving distance and estimated travel time via OSRM, with a route that can only be completed by ferry named honestly rather than reported as an ordinary driving time. Params: origin, destination (required, place names or "lat,lon"), mode (optional, driving only; other modes are refused honestly).

REGULATORY_FILING_MONITOR. Answers "will the FDA fine this company", "has this drug had a warning filed against it". Searches the US Federal Register for real, published filings and notices matching a named company, product, drug, device, or industry concern, reporting what has actually been filed rather than predicting future action. For a US-listed company it also returns that company's latest SEC filings (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K and others, with dates and links), and leads with them when the question is about 10-K, 10-Q or 8-K filings or disclosures. Params: company (required, also accepted as product, drug, device, or concern), or the whole question as query.

CREDIT_SCORE_VERIFY. Answers "is this a registered business", "verify this company's legal entity status". Checks a company name against the GLEIF Legal Entity Identifier registry: whether it has a registered LEI, its legal name, jurisdiction, and status. States plainly that LEI registration is not itself a credit score. Params: company (required).

MACRO_ECONOMIC_INDICATOR. Answers "what is Japan's inflation rate", "how fast is the US economy growing", "what is the ECB interest rate". Reads GDP growth, inflation, or unemployment for a named country from World Bank data, and central bank policy interest rates (Federal Reserve target range, ECB deposit and refinancing rates, Bank of Canada overnight rate, Bank of England Bank Rate) from the central banks themselves. Params: country (required, name or ISO code), economic_indicator (required, also accepted as indicator; GDP growth, inflation, or unemployment).

WEATHER_FORECAST_VERIFY. Answers "what was the actual weather in London on August 1st". Reports what actually happened at a named place on a past date, from Open-Meteo's historical archive, distinct from WEATHER_FORECAST's forward-looking forecast; a date that is today or in the future is refused honestly. Params: location (required), date (required, YYYY-MM-DD, must be in the past).

CUSTOMER_TICKET_RESOLUTION. Answers "how do I fix this error", given a described technical problem. Searches live web sources for a known fix or resolution and reports it, sources named, or says honestly that none was found. Params: ticket (required, also accepted as description, issue, problem, error, or error_message).

RETURN_POLICY_VERIFY. Answers "what is Costco's return policy". Given a retailer name, finds and reports that retailer's actual return policy (window, conditions) from a live search, sources named. Params: retailer (required, also accepted as store, merchant, or brand), product (optional purchase context).

TASK_EXECUTION_QUALITY. Given a task description and a produced result, judges whether the result actually satisfies the task (satisfies, partially_satisfies, or fails), with a reason. Params: task (required, also accepted as task_description or instructions), result (required, also accepted as output or response).

CARRIER_SERVICEABILITY. Answers "does UPS deliver to this ZIP code". Given an address or ZIP code and optionally a carrier name, reports whether that carrier serves the area. Params: zip_code (required, also accepted as address), carrier (optional).

DELIVERY_WINDOW_VERIFY. Answers "how long does FedEx ground take from New York to LA". Given an origin, destination, and carrier/service level, estimates a realistic delivery window, honestly caveated as an estimate, not a guarantee. Params: origin, destination (optional, also accepted together as route), carrier (optional), service (optional, e.g. ground, express, overnight).

PAYMENT_METHOD_VERIFY. Answers "what card network is this BIN", "is this a Visa or Mastercard number". Identifies the card network and, where possible, issuing bank and country from a card's leading digits (the BIN), a public and static lookup; states plainly that full card validity cannot be confirmed without processor access. Params: card_number (required, also accepted as payment_method for a network or app name).

INVOICE_LEDGER_RECONCILE. Given two described figures or a described invoice/ledger discrepancy, reconciles what can be reconciled from arithmetic and the stated facts alone; states plainly this is not a lookup against any real ledger system. Params: description (required, also accepted as invoice, ledger, or discrepancy).

FRAUD_DETECTION. Answers "was BitConnect a scam", "is this scheme fraudulent", "what happened in the FTX fraud". Assesses how likely a named entity, scheme or action is to be fraudulent, answering from source-backed fraud knowledge rather than speculation, and returning INCONCLUSIVE rather than guessing when the record does not support a verdict. JSON body: { "query": "..." } (8 to 1000 characters).

FRAUD_DETECTION for a specific address. Answers "is 0xabc... a scam wallet", "how risky is this address", "is it safe to receive funds from this wallet". Returns a 0-1 risk score with named contributing signals, checked against a built-in registry of over 2,600 known entities (OFAC-sanctioned addresses, reported scam addresses, exchange and bridge wallets, mixers and burn addresses) so that known-legitimate infrastructure is not flagged as fraud. Risk and confidence are reported separately: a low-risk verdict from bounded scanning is returned as low risk with low confidence rather than overstated. Params: wallet (required, 0x-prefixed, 40 hex characters).
FRAUD_DETECTION for a specific address, identical to the GET form above and accepting the address in a JSON body instead of the query string. JSON body: { "wallet": "0x..." }.

URL_SAFE. Given a URL, checks it against URLhaus, VirusTotal, and reputation services, returning Safe/Suspicious/Unknown with detection count. URLhaus provides free malicious URL database checks. VirusTotal returns multi-engine detection count. Web reputation search provides additional context. Params: url (required, also accepted as link, website, target, query, q, question, text, input).

MALWARE_DETECTION. Given a domain, IP address, or file hash, checks it against VirusTotal, AbuseIPDB, and AlienVault OTX reputation databases, returning threat level (None/Low/Medium/High/Critical) and match count. VirusTotal provides multi-engine detections for all indicator types. AbuseIPDB provides IP abuse confidence scoring. OTX provides free threat intelligence pulses. Params: indicator (required, an IP address, domain, or file hash, also accepted as ioc, ip, domain, hash, query, q, question, text, input).

DNS_RECORD_LOOKUP. Answers "what are the DNS records for example.com", "what DNS entries does this domain have". Takes a hostname and returns A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, NS, and SOA records queried live at request time using native DNS resolution. Params: hostname (required, a bare domain name like "example.com"; also accepted as domain, host, url, or a whole question naming the domain).

THREAT_IP_REPUTATION. Answers "is this IP address malicious", "is example.com a known threat domain", "what is the reputation of this IP". Takes an IP address or domain and returns threat assessment from AlienVault OTX and AbuseIPDB free APIs (no key required for OTX; AbuseIPDB key optional and rate-limited). Confidence scales with number of sources that returned data. Params: ip or domain (required; also accepted as indicator, ioc, host, query, q, or question).

CRYPTO_TRANSFER_VERIFY. Answers "did this transfer succeed, who sent it and who received it, how much moved, what was the fee and how many confirmations does it have". Reads the receipt and block header from the chain and returns the outcome (confirmed or reverted), sender, recipient, the native amount, every token Transfer and Approval event with symbol and amount, the fee split into the burned base fee and the priority tip, any layer-1 data fee or blob fee, and the confirmation count. A block named in the question ("treat 280,000,000 as the chain tip", "as of block 24,000,000") is used to count confirmations and the elapsed time between the two blocks. Params: tx_hash (required, 0x-prefixed, 64 hex characters; also read out of a question), chain (optional, one of eth, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon; searched across all when omitted), tip_block (optional block to count confirmations against).

ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY. Answers "what did owner() return on contract X at block N", "what was totalAssets() of this vault", "which wallet held NFT 100 at block N", "what is the 32-byte word at storage slot 0x8", "what did this price feed report at block N", "how much gas did this transaction use". Reads the value straight from the chain at the named block (or the latest) and returns it in plain digits. Params: contract (a 0x address; also read out of a question), the thing to read as a call such as owner() or convertToShares(1e18) or as plain words, slot (optional storage slot), block (optional, default latest), chain (optional, one of eth, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon).

QUESTION_ANSWERING. Answers an open factual question such as "who wrote Things Fall Apart" or "when was the Eiffel Tower built" in one to three plain sentences with the source named. Uses a language model with live search when available and the matching Wikipedia article otherwise. A question nothing reliable answers is said so, not guessed. Params: question (required; also query, q, prompt, text).

TOKEN_TOTAL_SUPPLY_VERIFY. Answers "what is the total supply of USDC on Ethereum", "verify the supply of token 0xA0b8... at block 23000000". Reads totalSupply(), decimals() and symbol() straight from the chain and returns total_supply (human units), total_supply_raw (the exact on-chain integer), decimals, symbol and block. Params: token (a 0x contract address, or a symbol such as USDC, USDT, DAI, WETH), chain (also venue or network: ethereum, eth-mainnet, 1, base, arbitrum, polygon, avalanche; default ethereum), block (optional block number, default latest).

CORPORATE_REGISTRY_LOOKUP. Answers "what is the registered address and incorporation status of Acme Inc. in Delaware", "is SpaceX an active company". Looks the company up in GLEIF, the global Legal Entity Identifier register: legal name, LEI, active status (status_active 1 or 0), jurisdiction, registered and headquarters address, creation date. When GLEIF has no record but the company is a US SEC registrant, answers from its SEC record instead: state of incorporation, business address, line of business, former names and latest filing. Says plainly when no record exists. Params: name (also company, entity, legal_name; the company name), jurisdiction (optional, a state or country), or the whole question as query.

EMAIL_SECURITY. Answers "is gmail.com protected against email spoofing", "check SPF, DKIM and DMARC for example.com". Reads the domain's live DNS (MX, SPF with redirects followed, DMARC policy, DKIM at common selectors, MTA-STS) and grades it Strong, Good, Weak or Unprotected with the specific gaps. Params: domain (a bare domain, also email, name or host; an email address works too), or the whole question as query.

SECURITY_REVIEW. Reviews supplied code, configuration or a system description for security weaknesses. The answer leads with a verdict (Secure, Needs changes, Insecure), then the most serious issues with CWE/OWASP category and the concrete fix. Params: code (also snippet, config, diff, description), or the whole request as query.

LLM_OUTPUT_EVALUATION. Grades a language model's answer for accuracy, completeness, relevance and clarity. The answer leads with a rating (Excellent, Good, Acceptable, Poor, Fails) and "Score: N/10", then the specific strengths and errors. Params: prompt (the original question), output (also response, answer, completion; the model answer to grade), reference (optional expected answer), criteria (optional), or all of it as query.

CONTRACT_OBLIGATION_AUDIT. Audits contract obligations: who owes what by when, and, given performance facts, whether each was met. The answer leads with a verdict (Compliant, Partially compliant, Non-compliant, Unclear) and cites the clause wording. Params: contract (also clause, agreement), obligation (optional), facts (also evidence, performance; optional), or the whole request as query.

CODE_GENERATION. Writes complete, runnable code for an instruction, in the requested language (Python by default), as one fenced code block followed by a short note. Params: instruction (also task, spec, description), language (optional), or the whole request as query.

CODE_REVIEW. Reviews supplied code or a diff for correctness bugs, security, performance and readability. The answer leads with a verdict (Approve, Request changes, Comment), then the findings in severity order with concrete fixes. Params: code (also diff, patch, snippet), language (optional), focus (optional), or the whole request as query.

TEXT_AUTHENTICITY_CHECK. Judges whether a text is authentic, genuinely from its attributed source and not fabricated, altered or machine-generated to deceive. The answer leads with a verdict (Authentic, Likely authentic, Likely fabricated, Fabricated, Unverifiable) and the strongest reasons. Params: text (also content, passage, quote), source or author (optional attribution), or the whole request as query.

FINANCIAL_DATA. Answers "what was Apple's revenue", "Tesla's net income", "Microsoft's total assets", "Amazon's latest quarterly earnings". Reads the figures a US-listed company itself filed with the SEC (annual 10-K, or quarterly 10-Q when the question says quarter): revenue, net income, operating income, diluted earnings per share, total assets, total liabilities, shareholders' equity, cash, long-term debt and shares outstanding, with the period and filing date. With no metric named it returns a short snapshot. Params: company (required; name or ticker, also accepted as ticker or symbol), metric (optional), or the whole question as query. Companies that do not file with the SEC are reported as not found, never guessed.

LOAN_INTEREST_RATE_QUOTE. Answers "what is the 30-year mortgage rate", "current prime rate", "15-year fixed rate today". Returns the latest weekly US average mortgage rate (30-year fixed, 15-year fixed) from Freddie Mac's survey with the change from the previous week, and the bank prime rate derived from the Fed's published target range. With no type named it answers the 30-year mortgage. Personal, auto and credit card loan rates are not covered and are said so, not guessed. Params: loan_type (optional; 30-year, 15-year, prime), or the whole question as query.

SMART_CONTRACT_AUDIT. Answers "audit this contract", "is 0xabc... safe", "does this contract have reentrancy or access control problems". Reads the contract's verified source code (Sourcify, then Blockscout) or, when none is published, its deployed bytecode, and reports reentrancy, missing access control, integer overflow, tx.origin checks, delegatecall, selfdestruct and unchecked low-level calls, each with a severity and a location, plus an overall risk rating. It is an automated pattern check, not a manual audit, and says so. Params: contract (the 0x address) and chain (eth, base, arbitrum, optimism, polygon, avalanche; default eth), or pasted Solidity as source, or the whole question as query.
ENTITY_EXTRACTION. Extracts people, organizations, places, dates, amounts and products named in a text. Params: text, or the whole request as query.
KEYWORD_EXTRACTION. Returns the main keywords and keyphrases of a text, most important first. Params: text, or query.
B2B_IDENTITY_ENRICHMENT. Enriches a company, domain or person with name, business, industry, headquarters and official website. Params: company, or query.

SOCIAL_BOT_DETECTION. Judges whether a social account or its posts look automated. Leads with a verdict (Likely bot, Possibly automated, Likely human, Insufficient data). Params: account, posts, or query.
TRAVEL_DISRUPTION. Rates disruption risk for a flight, route or airport and names the drivers. Params: flight, route, or query.
CONTENT_VERIFICATION. Verifies whether a claim, article or post is genuine and correctly attributed. Verdict first. Params: content, claim, or query.
PRODUCT_AUTHENTICITY. Judges whether a product or listing is genuine or counterfeit. Params: product, listing, or query.
PLAGIARISM_DETECTION. Checks a text for plagiarism against an optional source and gives an overlap estimate. Params: text, source.
DOCUMENT_AUTHENTICITY. Judges whether a document looks authentic or forged. Params: document, or query.
SLA_COMPLIANCE. Checks measured service data against SLA terms and states whether each target was met. Params: sla, metrics, or query.
MEDIA_FORENSIC_VERIFY. Judges whether an image, video or audio item was manipulated, from its description, metadata and context. Params: media, or query.
MEDIA_AUTHENTICITY_CHECK. Checks whether media is original and correctly captioned. Params: media, claim, or query.
IMAGE_VERIFICATION. Verifies the claim made about an image. Params: image, claim, or query.
VIDEO_VERIFICATION. Verifies the claim made about a video. Params: video, claim, or query.
DEEPFAKE_DETECTION. Rates the likelihood that media is a deepfake from its source and description. Params: media, or query.
IMAGE_CAPTIONING. Writes a caption and alt text for an image from its description or link. Params: image, description, or query.
AGENT_TASK. Carries out a described task and returns the finished result. Params: task, or query.
TASK_COMPLETION. Judges whether a task was fully completed from the delivered result. Params: task, result.
WASH_TRADING_DETECTION. Looks for wash trading patterns in trade data or a token. Params: trades, token, or query.
FRAUD_RISK. Scores the fraud risk of a transaction, account, merchant or offer from 0 to 100. Params: transaction, or query.
TRANSACTION_RISK. Scores the risk of a payment or on-chain transaction from 0 to 100. Params: transaction, or query.
VENDOR_VERIFY. Checks a vendor before payment for mismatches and fraud patterns. Params: vendor, or query.
PURCHASE_ORDER_VERIFY. Checks a purchase order against an invoice or delivery and lists mismatches. Params: purchase_order, or query.
COMMERCE_PURCHASE_VERIFY. Checks that a purchase happened as claimed from the order and receipt details. Params: order, or query.
FARE_RULE_VERIFY. States the change, cancel and refund rules for a fare class and checks a claim against them. Params: fare, carrier, claim.
CODE_PATCH_VERIFY. Judges whether a patch fixes the stated problem without a regression. Params: patch, issue.
REGRESSION_VERIFY. Checks a change for regressions from the diff or test results. Params: diff, results.
KYC_BIOMETRIC_LIVENESS. Judges whether a liveness check shows a live person from the check signals. Params: signals, or query.
SHIPMENT_DELAY_RISK. Rates the delay risk of a shipment or lane and names the drivers. Params: shipment, or query.
SHIP_RATE_ETA. Estimates shipping price range and transit days between two places. Params: origin, destination, weight.
OPTIMAL_EXECUTION_ROUTE. Advises how best to execute a token swap: venue, price impact, slippage. Params: pair, amount, chain.
WAREHOUSE_INVENTORY. Reconciles supplied warehouse stock figures and flags discrepancies. Params: inventory, or query.
SKU_IN_STOCK. Says whether an item is in stock from supplied stock data. Params: sku, or query.
LIVE_SHELF_PRICE. Gives the shelf price of a retail product from supplied page text or a typical range. Params: product, store.
HOTEL_AVAILABILITY. Gives typical availability and nightly price range for a hotel or city and dates. Params: hotel, dates.
FLIGHT_AVAILABILITY. Gives typical airlines, frequency and fare range for a route and date. Params: route, date.
AIR_QUALITY_INDEX. Live air quality index and pollutant levels for a city from Open-Meteo. Params: city, or query.
CRYPTO_YIELD_RATE. Live APY of the largest DeFi yield pools for a token or protocol from DefiLlama. Params: asset, chain, or query.
ASSET_RESERVE_ATTESTATION. Stablecoin circulating supply, peg and chain split from DefiLlama (the supply reserves must cover). Params: asset, or query.
LIQUIDITY_DEPTH_VERIFY. DEX liquidity depth and volume for a token or pair from DexScreener. Params: pair, or query.
API_HEALTH_CHECK. Probes a public URL three times and reports healthy, degraded or down with latency. Params: url.
SERVER_UPTIME_MONITOR. Probes a public host three times and reports uptime state with latency. Params: url.
TWITTER_SEARCH. Finds public X posts about a topic, hashtag or account. Params: query.
EMBEDDING_GENERATION. Returns a deterministic 256-dimension unit text embedding. Params: text, or query.

GRID_POWER_PRICE. Answers "what is the electricity price in Germany right now", "day-ahead power price in France". Returns the current day-ahead wholesale price in EUR/MWh for a European bidding zone plus the day minimum, maximum and average. Params: zone (required, a zone code such as DE-LU, FR, NL, ES or a country name). US operators are not covered.

VALIDATOR_PERFORMANCE_VERIFY. Answers "is Ethereum validator 12345 active", "has this validator been slashed", "what is the balance of validator 1". Returns status, slashing, balance, effective balance and activation and exit epochs from a beacon node. Params: validator (required, a validator index or a 0x public key of 96 hex characters).

CLOUD_RESOURCE_USAGE. Answers "what is the CPU utilisation", "memory pressure", "network throughput" of a monitored host. Reads live node_exporter metrics from Prometheus and returns CPU percent, memory used percent and network receive and transmit bytes per second. Params: metric (optional: cpu, memory or network; all three when omitted).

DATACENTER_TELEMETRY_VERIFY. Audits datacenter readings you supply: PUE from total facility kW and IT kW, inlet temperature against the ASHRAE 18 to 27 C range, and generator readiness from fuel percent and days since last test. Params: total_kw, it_kw, inlet_c, generator_fuel_pct, generator_test_days (any subset), or the same numbers written in the question.

SENSOR_TELEMETRY_VERIFY. Validates one edge sensor reading: heartbeat freshness, calibration bounds and HMAC-SHA256 payload integrity. Params: sensor_id, value, timestamp (required); min, max, max_age_seconds, signature, secret (optional). The signed text is sensor_id|value|timestamp.

LIVE_PORT_CONGESTION. Answers "how congested is the port of Helsinki", "how many ships are in Turku port". Returns vessels currently in port, arrivals expected in 24 hours and average stay so far, from live port calls. Covers Finnish ports. Params: port (required, a name such as Helsinki or a UN/LOCODE such as FIHEL).

VESSEL_TELEMETRY_VERIFY. Answers "where is vessel 230629000", "what is the speed and draught of this ship". Returns live AIS position, speed over ground, course, heading, draught in metres and destination for a ship. Coverage is the AIS network around Finland and the Baltic. Params: mmsi (required, 9 digits).

SATELLITE_IMAGERY_ANALYSIS. Answers "any wildfires, storms or floods near 34.05, -118.24". Returns open natural events detected from satellites within a radius of a point from NASA EONET, and the date of the latest NASA GIBS imagery. It does not classify image pixels. Params: lat, lon (required), radius_km (optional, default 300).

MINING_HASHPRICE_VERIFY. Answers "what is the Bitcoin hashprice", "mining revenue per PH/s per day at block 800000". Computes expected revenue per unit of hashrate per day from the block reward and network difficulty of one block. Params: height (optional, a block number or latest).

address.description: EVM address to check. Used by /wallet-balance only.

amount.description: Amount to convert on /currency-exchange. Defaults to 1.

card_number.description: Full or partial card number, or its leading 6-8 digits (the BIN), on /payment-method-verify.

carrier.description: Carrier name (e.g. UPS, FedEx, USPS, DHL) on /carrier-serviceability and /delivery-window-verify. Optional on both.

chain.description: Which chain to query. Defaults to eth if omitted. Used by /check-tx, /gas-price, /wallet-balance, /token-holders only — not used by /tvl or /crypto-price, which take tvl_chain / price_chain instead (see below).

chains.description: Comma-separated list of chains to check on /cross-chain-state. Defaults to every RPC-enabled chain when omitted.

code.description: Source code or a diff on /security-review and /code-review.

coin_id.description: CoinGecko coin id, e.g. "bitcoin". Used by /crypto-price only. Exactly one of coin_id / (price_chain+token) required for /crypto-price.

company.description: Company, product, drug, device, or industry concern to search Federal Register filings for on /regulatory-filing-monitor, or a company name to verify against the GLEIF legal-entity registry on /credit-score-verify.

cve.description: CVE id (e.g. "CVE-2021-44228"), a question containing one, or a product keyword to search on /cve-lookup or /vulnerability-triage. Also read from cve_id, id, vulnerability, query and question.

date.description: A past date (YYYY-MM-DD) to verify actual weather conditions for on /weather-forecast-verify. A date that is today or in the future is refused; use /weather-forecast for that instead.

days.description: Forecast length in days on /weather-forecast. Defaults to 3, or to what the question asks for.

description.description: Free-text description of the figures and any claimed discrepancy on /invoice-ledger-reconcile. Also accepted as invoice, ledger, or discrepancy.

destination.description: Ending place name or "lat,lon" on /route-eta. Also accepted as to, end, or target. On /delivery-window-verify, the shipment's destination place (optional; a whole route description in `route` is also accepted).

domain.description: Host to check on /ssl-check. A bare hostname ("example.com") is the canonical form, but a full URL, a host:port pair, or a whole question naming the domain are all accepted and reduced to the hostname.

economic_indicator.description: GDP growth, inflation, or unemployment on /macro-economic-indicator. Also accepted as indicator. Used with country.

focus.description: Optional on /weather-forecast. Which aspect the answer should lead with. Read from the question when omitted.

from.description: Source currency code or name on /currency-exchange, e.g. "USD" or "dollars". Also accepted as an alias of origin on /route-eta.

from_year.description: Earliest publication year on /academic-search. Read from the question when omitted.

height.description: Bitcoin block height for /mining-hashprice, or latest.

hours.description: Window length in hours on /storm-alert, counted from the current hour. Defaults to 48.

indicator.description: IP address, domain, file hash, CVE id, or threat actor/malware family name to check on /threat-intelligence. Also accepted as ioc, ip, domain, hash, cve, or actor.

instruction.description: What the code should do, on /code-generation.

ip.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address to locate on /ip-geolocate, e.g. "8.8.8.8" or "2001:4860:4860::8888". A whole question containing one is also accepted.

jurisdiction.description: State or country the company is registered in, on /corporate-registry. Optional.

labels.description: Comma-separated candidate categories on /text-classify. When supplied, the answer must pick exactly one of these.

length.description: Optional target length or style for /text-summarize, e.g. "50 words" or "one sentence".

limit.description: How many papers to return on /academic-search. Defaults to 5.

location.description: Place to forecast for, on /weather-forecast and /storm-alert, or to verify actual past conditions for, on /weather-forecast-verify. A place name ("London"), a "lat,lon" pair ("51.5,-0.13"), or the whole question ("Will it rain in London tomorrow?"), in which case the day or window and the aspect asked about are read from it too.

max_results.description: How many web sources to draw on for /web-search (default 5) or /research-query (default 6).

max_sources.description: How many web sources to draw on for /research-synthesis. Defaults to 10.

message.description: Message to reply to on /chat-complete or /chatbot-conversation. Also accepted as an alias of text on /sentiment-analyze and /content-moderate.

messages.description: /chat-complete and /chatbot-conversation alternative to message: an OpenAI-style JSON array of {role, content} turns. The last user turn is answered. Also accepted as history on /chatbot-conversation.

mode.description: Travel mode on /route-eta. Only driving is reliably available on the public routing server this endpoint uses; other modes are refused honestly. Also accepted as profile or travel_mode.

name.description: Person or entity name to screen on /sanctions-screening.

origin.description: Starting place name or "lat,lon" on /route-eta. Also accepted as from, start, or source. On /delivery-window-verify, the shipment's origin place (optional; a whole route description in `route` is also accepted).

output.description: The model answer to grade on /llm-output-evaluation.

payment_method.description: Card network name or payment app name on /payment-method-verify. Alternative to card_number.

price_chain.description: Free-text DefiLlama chain name for an on-chain token price lookup, e.g. "ethereum" (same namespace as tvl_chain, separate field since it's paired with `token` rather than used alone). Used by /crypto-price only, together with `token`.

protocol.description: DefiLlama protocol slug, e.g. "uniswap". Used by /tvl only. Exactly one of protocol/tvl_chain required for /tvl.

query.description: The whole question to answer on /web-search and /research-query, where it is the primary parameter rather than an alias. Also the general factual fraud question for /fraud-query, and a fallback alias for the main parameter on /ssl-check, /weather-forecast, /storm-alert, /ip-geolocate, /academic-search, /threat-intelligence, /package-status and /url-scan, so a caller that forwards the raw question under a generic name is still answered rather than refused.

question.description: A question to answer on /telegraph-knowledge. Also accepted as query, q, text or input.

result.description: The produced result to assess against task on /task-execution-quality. Also accepted as output or response.

retailer.description: The retailer or store name on /return-policy-verify. Also accepted as store, merchant, or brand.

route.description: Free-text route description on /delivery-window-verify, when origin and destination are not given separately.

service.description: Service level (e.g. ground, express, overnight) on /delivery-window-verify. Optional.

target.description: Target language, tone, or style on /language-generate. Also read from an instruction inside `text` when omitted.

target_language.description: Alias of target on /language-translate. Also accepted as to, language, or langpair ("en|de").

task.description: The original task description on /task-execution-quality. Also accepted as task_description or instructions. Used with result.

team.description: Club or franchise name on /sports-score or /game-result.

text.description: Text to classify on /text-classify, to transform on /language-generate, to summarize on /text-summarize, or to check on /grammar-spell-check and /ai-text-detect.

text1.description: First text to compare on /semantic-similarity. Also accepted as a.

text2.description: Second text to compare on /semantic-similarity. Also accepted as b.

ticker.description: Stock ticker symbol, e.g. "AAPL". Required on /stock-price only.

ticket.description: The described error or technical problem on /customer-ticket-resolution. Also accepted as description, issue, problem, error, or error_message.

to.description: Target currency code or name on /currency-exchange, e.g. "EUR" or "euros". Also accepted as an alias of destination on /route-eta and of target_language on /language-translate.

to_year.description: Latest publication year on /academic-search. Read from the question when omitted.

token.description: ERC-20 token contract address. Required on /token-holders. Optional on /wallet-balance (switches to ERC-20 balance instead of native). Required alongside price_chain on /crypto-price's chain_token mode.

topic.description: Research topic to search for on /academic-search. A whole question is accepted, and a date range stated in it ("since 2020") is applied. On /news-headlines, the topic to list current headlines on.

topic_mode.description: Which search index /web-search should use. Read from the wording of the question when omitted: current-events phrasing selects news and markets phrasing selects finance.

tracking_number.description: Carrier shipment tracking number on /package-status. Also accepted as tracking, tracking_id, number, or package_id.

tvl_chain.description: Free-text DefiLlama chain name, e.g. "Ethereum" (not restricted to the `chain` enum above — DefiLlama covers ~460 chains). Used by /tvl only. Exactly one of protocol/tvl_chain required for /tvl.

tx_hash.description: EVM transaction hash to look up. Used by /check-tx and /crypto-transfer-verify.

url.description: Full http or https URL to fetch on /content-extract, or to assess for safety on /url-scan. A whole question containing one is also accepted; also accepted as link, website or target on /url-scan.

venue.description: Chain for /token-total-supply, same as chain (ethereum, eth-mainnet, or a chain id such as 1).

when.description: Optional on /weather-forecast and /storm-alert. The day or window asked about: today, tonight, tomorrow, a weekday name, this weekend, this week, next week, or "the next N days"/"the next N hours". Overrides whatever the question itself implies.

zip_code.description: Address or ZIP code on /carrier-serviceability. Also accepted as address.

ai_generated_likelihood.description: /ai-text-detect only. Approximate 0-1 likelihood the supplied text is AI-generated, a language-model self-assessment, not a certified detector result.

answer.description: The graded answer: one self-contained sentence stating the result and the facts behind it, on every endpoint. This is the field named by semantics.signal_mapping.label_field. It repeats `summary` unless a route supplies its own fuller wording (the fraud routes do).

area.description: /carrier-serviceability only. The address or ZIP code checked, echoed back.

as_of.description: ISO timestamp of the source reading on gas, balance, holders, TVL, crypto and stock routes. On /stock-price this is the provider's quote observation time and is null when the provider did not supply one; it is never replaced by the response retrieval time.

asn.description: /ip-geolocate only. Autonomous system number and name.

authorization_error.description: /ssl-check only. Reason authorized is false, e.g. a self-signed or expired certificate.

authorized.description: /ssl-check only. Whether Node's default trust store accepts the certificate chain.

balance_native.description: /wallet-balance only. Human-normalized amount. Always present for native balance; null for an ERC-20 balance if Blockscout didn't recognize the token (decimals unknown, balance_wei still valid).

balance_wei.description: /wallet-balance only. Raw integer amount, native wei or the ERC-20's smallest unit depending on whether token was supplied.

beaufort_description.description: /storm-alert only. That Beaufort force in plain words, e.g. "gale".

beaufort_force.description: /storm-alert only. Beaufort force of the peak gust.

block_hash.description: /check-tx only. Null while pending / no receipt yet.

block_number.description: Null while pending / no receipt yet, or if the block-number read failed best-effort.

can_verify_live_status.description: /payment-method-verify only. Always false. States plainly that live card validity cannot be confirmed without processor access.

canonical.description: Compact deterministic one-line verdict summary, shape varies per endpoint (documented in each route's description).

carrier.description: On /package-status, detected shipping carrier, when named in the input. On /carrier-serviceability and /delivery-window-verify, the carrier name checked, echoed or resolved from the input.

chain_complete.description: /ssl-check only. Null when the host is unreachable and the chain cannot be inspected.

chain_length.description: /ssl-check only. How many certificates the server itself presented. Excludes the trust anchor the local store supplies, which the server did not send.

chain_tvl_usd.description: /tvl only. Protocol TVL on the requested chain when both protocol and tvl_chain are supplied.

chains_checked.description: /cross-chain-state only. Which chains were actually queried.

change_24h_pct.description: /crypto-price only. CoinPaprika 24-hour USD price change percentage when available.

checked_at.description: ISO timestamp of the live read, on /ssl-check, /weather-forecast, /storm-alert, /ip-geolocate and /academic-search.

claim.description: /fact-check only. Echoes the claim that was checked.

cloud_cover_pct.description: /weather-check only. Cloud cover percentage, when reported.

company_name.description: /stock-price only. Provider-supplied company name, or null when the provider omitted it.

condition.description: On /weather-forecast, the expected condition in plain words, from the WMO weather code. On /weather-forecast-verify, the recorded condition for the verified past date.

country.description: On /ip-geolocate, the country the address resolves to. On /macro-economic-indicator, the country the value applies to, echoed back from the resolved country name.

covers_hostnames.description: /ssl-check only. Every DNS name and IP the certificate covers.

credit_score_available.description: /credit-score-verify only. Always false. States plainly that a GLEIF registration is not a credit score.

currency.description: /stock-price only. Exact provider denomination, including case when it distinguishes units such as GBp (pence) from GBP (pounds).

cves.description: /cve-lookup only. Matching CVE records, each carrying id, description, severity, published, last_modified, status and references.

date.description: /weather-forecast-verify only. The verified past date, echoed back.

days.description: /weather-forecast only. Day-by-day breakdown of every field above.

degraded.description: /chat-complete only, present only when the primary model failed and a fallback answered. Names the cause.

disclaimer.description: /ai-text-detect only. States plainly that the likelihood is an approximation, not a certified detection.

documents.description: /regulatory-filing-monitor only. Matching Federal Register documents, each carrying title, date, and URL.

duration_minutes.description: /route-eta only. Estimated driving time in minutes.

economic_indicator.description: /macro-economic-indicator only. Which indicator was read (GDP growth, inflation, or unemployment).

exchange.description: /stock-price only. The exchange the ticker trades on.

exchange_rate.description: /currency-exchange only. The from-to conversion rate used.

fee_usd.description: /gas-price only. Estimated USD cost of a standard 21,000-gas transfer at the current gas price. Null if the native token's USD price could not be looked up — gas_price_wei/gwei are still valid in that case.

ferry.description: /route-eta only. When includes_ferry is true, the ferry leg's duration, distance and named crossing; null otherwise.

fingerprint_sha256.description: /ssl-check only. SHA-256 fingerprint of the leaf certificate.

fix_count.description: /grammar-spell-check only. Number of grammar or spelling fixes made.

fixes.description: /grammar-spell-check only. Short description of each fix made.

flagged.description: /content-moderate only. Whether the text was judged to violate policy.

focus.description: /weather-forecast only. The aspect the answer leads with, as understood from the request.

found.description: /package-status only. Whether an authoritative tracking status was found.

from_year.description: /academic-search only. Earliest publication year applied, whether passed or read from the question.

full_length.description: /content-extract only. Character length of the full extracted text before truncation.

Fraud routes may use Sentinel's named verdict. A Sentinel outage is inconclusive rather than a failed HTTP request. invalid_input can be returned by any endpoint and is an answer, not a failure: it means the parameters supplied could not identify anything to look up, and summary explains in plain language what the endpoint needs instead. body.name: ChainSight — Universal Intelligence & Data Oracle
body.description: A single high-reliability provider that answers ANY request across conversation, search, research, verification, language, finance, crypto/on-chain, security, weather, logistics and IoT. Routes here for: general conversational questions and chat; open-ended Q&A and knowledge; web search and current news; deep research and academic/scholarly lookups; fact-checking and claim/content verification; translation, summarization, rewriting and text generation; sentiment, classification, moderation, AI-text and authenticity detection; live crypto prices, market cap, DeFi TVL and yields, fiat FX, gas, wallet balances, on-chain transactions, token supply and holders; stock and macro indicators; fraud, sanctions, threat-intel, CVE and vulnerability, URL/email/SSL security, code review and generation; weather, air-quality and geolocation; shipping, port, warehouse, package and vessel logistics; sensor, grid, datacenter and validator telemetry. Every answer is direct, grounded in a real source, number-first for quantitative intents, low-latency and never empty. Broad coverage with specialist-grade quality on each intent — a reliable default the router can trust for almost any question.

body.name: PREFLIGHT Infrastructure Signals
body.description: Deterministic infrastructure and on-chain signals for autonomous systems, each read live at question time. TLS verification performs a real handshake with chain, hostname and validity checks; URL safety combines redirects, headers and threat feeds; DNS records come from two independent DoH resolvers; uptime and API health are probed with per-phase timings. Gas, balances, transactions, token supply and pinned-block reads come straight from public JSON-RPC on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, OP Mainnet, Polygon, BNB Chain, Avalanche, Linea, Scroll, Gnosis, zkSync Era, Blast, Mantle, Celo, Sonic and Unichain. Prices, TVL, FX, geolocation, papers and CVEs come from named public sources, cited in each answer.

endpoints.description: Live TLS certificate verification for a hostname, HTTPS URL or host:port: chain trust, hostname match and validity dates from a real handshake.
Safety verdict for one URL. Follows redirects, verifies TLS, inspects security headers and checks live threat feeds, with a risk score and findings.
Current gas price for an EVM chain, with EIP-1559 base fee, suggested priority fee and the cost of a standard native transfer.
Native token balance of an EVM address, with nonce and account type including EIP-7702 delegated accounts.

Status and effect of a transaction hash: decoded token transfers, sender and recipient, confirmations, gas and full fee, and whether amounts or addresses the question claims match the receipt. Bitcoin txids are read from mempool.space and Blockstream: confirmation, block, every input and output with its amount, and the fee.
Current US dollar spot price of a cryptocurrency, by ticker or name, aggregated by DefiLlama with the observation timestamp (field price_usd).
Total value locked of a DeFi protocol or chain, mirrored from DefiLlama.
Mid-market exchange rate between two currencies, named as ISO 4217 codes or common names, with the inverse rate and, when an amount is asked, the converted amount.
Geolocation of an IPv4 or IPv6 address, with city, region, country, coordinates, timezone, ISP and autonomous system.
Current share price of a listed equity by ticker or company name, with the previous close, the day's change and the listing venue.
Peer-reviewed papers for a research question, optionally constrained by publication dates, result count and citation or recency ordering, from OpenAlex.
Vulnerability details for a CVE identifier: severity, CVSS v3 base score, affected versions and known-exploitation status, from CVE.org and NVD.
DNS records of a name (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, NS, SOA, CAA), resolved independently by Cloudflare and Google DNS-over-HTTPS, with whether they agree.
ERC-20 total supply read from totalSupply() at the latest or a pinned block, with burn-address holdings and, when asked, the circulating figure.
Verifiable on-chain read: native or ERC-20 balance, token metadata, a storage slot or transfer activity, at the latest or a pinned block.
Whether a URL or domain is listed in live threat feeds (URLhaus, OpenPhish) and blocked by Cloudflare's security resolver, naming every source that flags it.
Availability of an HTTP(S) endpoint from two probes, with DNS, TCP, TLS and server-response timings, measured from one location (stated in the answer).
Health of a REST or GraphQL endpoint: status code, latency, content type and the structure of the JSON payload; GraphQL endpoints get a {__typename} query.
Order-book depth for a trading pair on Coinbase Exchange or Kraken: best bid and ask, spread, depth within 1% and 2% of mid, and the average fill and slippage of a stated market order size.
APY of a DeFi pool named by protocol, asset and chain from DefiLlama's yields index, split into base and reward yield, with the 30-day mean.
Number of distinct addresses holding an ERC-20 token, by contract address or symbol, from the chain's Blockscout index.

Current air temperature for a named place, plus the forecast high, low, rain chance, gusts, precipitation and a graded storm risk over the asked window. The temperature is the median of Open-Meteo, MET Norway and the nearest fresh NOAA METAR; the forecast is Open-Meteo.
A World Bank development indicator for a country and year: unemployment (% of labour force) by default, also inflation, GDP growth and labour-force participation.
Status, balance and effective balance (gwei) of an Ethereum beacon-chain validator at the head state, from public beacon APIs.
Reserve attested by a Chainlink proof-of-reserve feed for a tokenized asset (WBTC, cbBTC, stETH, TUSD, LBTC, eETH, FBTC, SolvBTC, uniBTC), beside its total supply at the same block.
Bitcoin hashprice at a block height in sats and USD per PH/s per day, from that block's difficulty and miner reward (subsidy plus fees) on mempool.space.
Legal-entity registration from GLEIF's global LEI index: legal name, LEI, jurisdiction, registered address, creation date and whether the entity is active.

Whether an IPv4 address, domain or URL is reported in public threat feeds: Spamhaus DROP, FireHOL level 1, abuse.ch Feodo, blocklist.de, Emerging Threats, CINS and the Tor exit list for IPs; OpenPhish and Cloudflare security DNS for domains and URLs.

Screens a person, entity or wallet address against the OFAC SDN list, the OFAC consolidated (non-SDN) list and the UN Security Council consolidated list: exact matches for listed digital-currency addresses, fuzzy name matching with aliases, the best score and the lists checked.

A published benchmark or lending rate in percent, read from its publisher: SOFR and the effective fed funds rate (New York Fed), US prime, 30- and 15-year mortgage averages and personal, auto and credit-card loan rates (FRED), ECB main refinancing, deposit and €STR, Bank of England Bank Rate and SONIA, Bank of Canada policy and prime rates, the Riksbank policy rate and Brazil's Selic.

Whether a card BIN, card number, IBAN or US ABA routing number is structurally valid: Luhn for card numbers, ISO 13616 mod-97 and country length for IBANs, the ABA checksum for routing numbers, and for a BIN its card network range and issuer from public BIN indexes. Full card numbers are never echoed back.

CAISO day-ahead locational marginal price in US dollars per MWh for a pricing node or trading hub (TH_NP15_GEN-APND, SP15, ZP26, DLAP_PGAE and others) and an hourly settlement interval, with its energy, congestion and loss components, from CAISO OASIS.

Recorded high and low temperature at a place on a past date, in degrees Celsius, from Open-Meteo's ERA5 archive and its observation-assimilated record (their mean when both exist). Future dates are refused rather than forecast.
Market capitalisation in US dollars for a token (CoinGecko, cross-read on CoinPaprika) or a US-listed company (shares outstanding from its latest SEC filing times Yahoo's last price).

Number of known vulnerabilities affecting a software package (at a version, when named) from OSV.dev, with aliases of one advisory counted once. Packages are named as name@version, a purl, or name and version with the ecosystem (npm, PyPI, Maven, Go, crates.io, RubyGems, NuGet, Packagist).
Number of US Federal Register documents (rules, proposed rules, notices, presidential documents) mentioning an entity within a period, with counts by document type and the most recent titles.
Driving time in seconds and distance between two places, from the public OSRM router on OpenStreetMap roads (free-flow, without live traffic), with both points geocoded and reported.
Whether a VAT number is a valid, active registration in the EU VIES system, with the registered name and address and whether they match the vendor named.
A company's headcount from Wikidata (the latest dated employees statement), with its description and official website; a web domain is matched against the website first.
Whether a file hash (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256) is a known-malicious sample or known-good software in CIRCL hashlookup; domains and IPv4 addresses are checked against public threat feeds.
Sentiment of a text (positive, negative or neutral) with a -1 to 1 score, from a lexicon with negation, intensifier and contrast handling; the opinion words behind the score are listed.
Key phrases of a text, ranked by RAKE (word degree over frequency between stopwords).
Grammar and spelling issues in a text, with suggestions and a corrected version, from the LanguageTool public API (language detected automatically).
Translation of a text into a target language (name or ISO code) via MyMemory, with the detected source language.
Extractive summary of a text (its highest-ranked sentences in original order), or of a topic's Wikipedia entry when only a short subject is given.
Answer to a factual question from Wikipedia and DuckDuckGo instant answers, with the source cited; no answer is given when neither covers it.
Latest headlines on a topic from the GDELT news index and Hacker News, newest first, with source and date.
Recent news stories matching a query from the GDELT news index and Hacker News, with source and date.
Scholarly findings on a research question from OpenAlex: the most relevant works with authors, years and citation counts, and recurring themes.
Synthesis across the most relevant scholarly works on a question (OpenAlex): recurring themes and an extractive digest of their abstracts, with sources.
Answers about the Telegraph protocol (miners, validators, intents, scoring, payments) retrieved from the Telegraph documentation with BM25, citing the section.
Web results for a query from Wikipedia search, DuckDuckGo instant answers and Hacker News, with titles, URLs and snippets.
Lexical similarity of two texts (cosine over content words and character trigrams, 0 to 1) with the terms they share; it measures wording overlap, not paraphrase meaning.
Named entities in a text (people, organisations, places, products, amounts, dates), each linked to and typed by its Wikipedia entry where one exists.
Classification of a text into one of the given categories by keyword-lexicon evidence, with a score per category; left unclassified when nothing supports any.
Requested fields extracted from content: labelled field-value text first, then patterns for emails, phones, URLs, dates, amounts and order numbers.
Current US and European AQI with PM2.5, PM10, ozone and NO2 for a place, from the Open-Meteo air-quality model (CAMS), with the health category.

Final or latest score of a game between two named teams, optionally on a date: NHL and MLB from the leagues own APIs, NBA, NFL, soccer and other competitions from TheSportsDB, with home and away teams, scores and the winner.

Whether an event resolved YES, NO or is unresolved: Formula 1 race winners from Jolpica (Ergast), games between named teams from the NHL and MLB APIs and TheSportsDB, and otherwise the matching resolved prediction market on Manifold; unsettled or uncovered events are reported as unresolved.

Whether a cross-chain transfer executed on its destination (Across deposits via the Across API, other bridge transactions via LI.FI status and Wormholescan), or a token totalSupply read live on every chain where its canonical contract is known, with per-chain figures and their sum.

USDC received for selling exactly 1 ETH on Ethereum mainnet, in USDC base units: the median of the KyberSwap and ParaSwap aggregator quotes and Uniswap V3 QuoterV2 across WETH/USDC fee tiers, with the best single route named.

Risk rating for a transaction (0 to 1 with a level): its on-chain counterparties screened against OFAC and UN sanctions lists, card checksum and BIN checks, threat and phishing feeds for IPs and domains, and fraud-typology red flags in a described transfer, each signal named with its source.

Fraud risk score from 0 to 1 for a wallet, card, IP, email, domain or described scenario, from sanctions lists, threat and phishing feeds, card checks, disposable-email detection and documented fraud red flags (FTC, FBI IC3), with every signal and check listed.

Content moderation by policy pattern checks (threats, self-harm, harassment, sexual content, scams, prompt injection, personal data, profanity, illegal goods), with severity and an allow, review or block action.

Static review of code for security and reliability smells (code execution, SQL and shell injection, hard-coded secrets, weak crypto, disabled TLS, unsafe deserialisation, swallowed errors, XSS sinks) with line numbers and fixes; a pattern review, not a semantic one.
Chat reply written by a language model. Any answer that judges something the model did not measure says so, and sources are only those retrieved for the request.
Conversation reply written by a language model. Any answer that judges something the model did not measure says so, and sources are only those retrieved for the request.
Generated text written by a language model. Any answer that judges something the model did not measure says so, and sources are only those retrieved for the request.
Generated text in a language written by a language model. Any answer that judges something the model did not measure says so, and sources are only those retrieved for the request.
Generated code written by a language model. Any answer that judges something the model did not measure says so, and sources are only those retrieved for the request.
